plan_a_advantages: More frequent and focused hill sessions to build trail-specific power.
Longer endurance runs (85 min) to improve overall trail running capacity.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated strength and mobility session, addressing important aspects of injury prevention and biomechanics.
Longer, moderate-intensity run (110 min) which could be beneficial for some runners, though less effective for speed development.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted hill work and longer endurance runs, crucial for trail-specific speed development. While Plan B includes strength and mobility work, it lacks the focused intensity needed to build the necessary power and efficiency for trail running. Plan A’s consistent aerobic base building, combined with dedicated hill sessions, will more effectively translate to improved speed and stamina on technical trails. Plan B’s longer run is also at a moderate intensity, which is less effective for building the kind of sustained effort required for faster trail times.
